Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Vendr proof origination & sampling scope — CAIQ/SIG traceability

Hi Claire,

Thanks for the kickoff call last week. As we begin onboarding NovumCloud into Vendr we need a short, auditable sample set that proves field-level origin for a handful of CAIQ/SIG mappings so our SOC 2 evidence owners can validate claims. Specifically we need: 

- A small manifest (CSV) of 8–12 evidence items that align to the CAIQ/SIG fields listed below. For each item, indicate provenance: generated-by-vendr, uploaded-by-customer, s3-presign, or signed-attachment.
- Hash (SHA256) and timestamp for each item plus a URL or presigned S3 link (if applicable).
- One example of a KMS rotation record, one example of disk-encryption-at-rest proof, and one example of a SOC 2 control evidence doc (e.g., monitoring alert runbook) mapped to SIG identifier.

Preferred delivery: upload to the Vendr claim (link in footer) or share presigned S3 URLs. We don't need the full portal bundle—just the minimal, traceable proof artifacts so our compliance team can confirm mapping and acceptance criteria.

Target timeline: can you provide the sample manifest + artifacts by EOD Friday (2028-05-08)? If presigns are easier we can accept a short-lived window (48 hours).

Thanks — I'll loop Jordan in to help with the mapping spreadsheet.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Security Intake Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-field-list.txt (attached locally as reference)
Link: https://vendr.io/portal/claim/57821

Thanks Soojin — happy to help. A couple quick clarifying questions before we assemble the package: 

1) For the KMS rotation record, do you need the key metadata + change log, or a signed attestation from NovumCloud's ops team? We can include both but want to know which the auditor prefers.
2) For the SOC 2 control doc, would a timestamped runbook export (PDF) be sufficient, or do you require an export that includes the event IDs referenced in the control (i.e. matching alert hashes)?
3) CSV manifest format: we can provide columns [filename, sha256, origin, uploaded_at, proof_url, vendr_claim_id]. Is that acceptable?

If that format works we'll aim to drop a ZIP with 10 artifacts and the manifest into the claim. If presigned URLs are preferred, I can generate 48-hour presigns and include them in the manifest. Give me permission to include signed attachments (we can PGP-sign if that helps with chain-of-custody).

Claire Park
Customer Success — Vendr
claire@vendr.io

Soojin — thanks. Short notes from compliance: 

- Manifest format Claire proposed is fine. Make sure 'origin' uses one of our canonical values (vendr, customer-upload, s3-presign, signed-attachment).
- For KMS rotation: we want the key metadata + rotation entry (timestamp + actor) and either the aggr hash or a signed attestation. The rotation entry should show the key ID and the rotation date.
- For encryption-at-rest: a storage provider statement (or disk header export) plus an object-level hash is sufficient.
- For SOC2 artifacts: prefer runbook PDF plus a correlating event id list; auditors will spot-check the event ids against our logs.

Jordan — can you populate the mapping sheet with SIG identifiers we should validate (I'll DM the exact list). Aim to have the XLSX with field-to-CAIQ mapping by Tuesday so Claire can slot files into the manifest.

Marissa
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
